title: Robustness of the deterministic consensus hierarchy
formal: Can combining deterministic shared-object types yield a wait-free consensus number strictly larger than the maximum consensus number of the types used separately?
definitions: The intended hierarchy permits any number of instances of a type and atomic read/write registers. Its consensus number is the largest process count for which deterministic wait-free binary consensus can be implemented; it is infinite when all finite counts are possible. Combining types means allowing instances of each type in one implementation. Wait freedom requires completion after finitely many steps of each participating nonfaulty process regardless of other process speeds or crashes. The target excludes nondeterministic shared objects.

context_blocks.text: Consensus number measures the synchronization power of a shared-memory primitive. Robustness asks whether that power composes: can several individually weak primitive types jointly become stronger?

The book distinguishes the refined hierarchy used here from an earlier nonrobust version. Counterexamples using nondeterministic objects also do not settle the deterministic question. The hierarchy’s definition is therefore part of the mathematical problem, not a terminology choice.

why: Determine whether a central measure of synchronization power behaves consistently under composition.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, with the specified quantifiers, model and guarantees. A conditional theorem settles only that conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.
